company_name: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC Limited

about_company.about_short: Runs Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund and earns fees on its assets, plus PMS, AIF, offshore and government mandates.
about_company.business_intro: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC manages the Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund and smaller PMS, AIF, real estate and offshore businesses. Investors pay a fee that is a percentage of the assets managed, highest on equity funds. Asset management and advisory fees were 93.7% of consolidated fee income in FY26 and PMS and other services the other 6.3%.
about_company.about_long: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC is the investment manager of Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund; Aditya Birla Capital held 44.89% and Sun Life 29.93% at 31 March 2026. It earns a fee on the average assets it manages, and the rate depends on the asset class: about 62-63 basis points on equity, 24-25 on debt and 12-13 on liquid funds in Q4 FY26. Mutual fund average AUM was ₹4,418 bn in Q2 FY27, up 4% year on year, of which equity was ₹2,092 bn. Beyond mutual funds it runs PMS, AIF, real estate and offshore funds, a specialised investment fund (Apex SIF) and a GIFT City subsidiary. It also manages the ESIC and EPFO debt mandates: ₹6,528 bn of Q2 FY27 average AUM that takes the reported total to ₹11,056 bn but earns very little; without them AUM was ₹4,528 bn. Fees from PMS and other services were 6.3% of consolidated fee income in FY26.

company_timeline.title: Incorporated as Birla Capital International AMC
company_timeline.detail: Set up by the Aditya Birla Group and the Capital Group; Aditya Birla Capital and Sun Life (India) AMC Investments are now the promoters.

company_timeline.title: Lists on NSE and BSE
company_timeline.detail: Shares listed on 11 October 2021. In March 2024 the promoters sold 11.16% through an offer for sale on the exchanges to meet the 25% public-shareholding rule.

company_timeline.title: Starts managing the ESIC debt mandate
company_timeline.detail: The ESIC debt portfolio was ₹7,456 crore for the quarter ended 31 March 2025. Management says mandate revenue is very marginal.

company_timeline.title: Incorporates a GIFT City IFSC subsidiary
company_timeline.detail: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC International (IFSC) Limited became a wholly owned subsidiary on 4 December 2025 and later received a retail licence.

company_timeline.title: Launches Apex SIF, its specialised investment fund
company_timeline.detail: The first offering was the Apex SIF Hybrid Long-Short Fund, reported on the Q4 FY26 call.

company_timeline.title: Takes on the EPFO debt mandate
company_timeline.detail: EPFO picked the company to manage part of its debt portfolio for five years; about ₹6.08 lakh crore came in during Q1 FY27 and closing total AUM passed ₹10 lakh crore on 30 June 2026.

business_facts.title: Individual investors hold half of mutual fund AUM
business_facts.text: Individual investors' monthly average AUM was ₹2,177 bn in September 2026, 50% of mutual fund AUM, up from 48% in September 2025; the rest is institutional money. The fund served 11.4 million folios at 30 September 2026.

business_facts.title: Smaller (B-30) cities are about 18% of mutual fund AUM
business_facts.text: Monthly average AUM from beyond the top 30 cities was ₹780 bn in September 2026, 17.9% of mutual fund AUM (17.5% a year earlier). Over 80% of its 310+ locations are in B-30 cities. Offshore funds averaged ₹51 bn of AUM in Q2 FY27. The company gives no revenue split by region.

business_facts.title: 96,000+ distributors and 90+ banks sell its funds
business_facts.text: Over 96,000 KYD-compliant mutual fund distributors, 360+ national distributors and 90+ banks, served through 310+ locations, plus 130+ digital partners.

sources.label: Q2 FY27 investor presentation and press release (21 Oct 2026)

business_facts.title: Fee rates differ about fivefold by asset class
business_facts.text: Management put yields at about 62-63 basis points on equity, 24-25 on debt and 12-13 on liquid funds in Q4 FY26, and 63-64 on equity in Q1 FY27. Equity was 47.4% of mutual fund average AUM in Q2 FY27, so it carries more of the fee income than its AUM share.

sources.label: Q2 FY27 investor presentation and press release (21 Oct 2026)

business_facts.title: Government mandates lift AUM but add little revenue
business_facts.text: The ESIC (from Q4 FY25) and EPFO (from Q1 FY27) debt mandates were ₹6,528 bn of Q2 FY27 average AUM, taking the total to ₹11,056 bn, up 140% year on year, while mutual fund AUM rose 4% to ₹4,418 bn. Management calls the mandate revenue very marginal.

sources.label: Q2 FY27 investor presentation and press release (21 Oct 2026)

business_facts.title: Equity fund market share fell every quarter since Q3 FY24
business_facts.text: Equity mutual fund market share (excluding ETFs) fell from 5.0% in Q3 FY24 to 4.06% in Q4 FY26 and 3.92% in Q2 FY27. Overall mutual fund share fell from 7.1% to 5.69% over the same quarters.

Q4 FY26 investor presentation and press release

what_changed.headline: PMS and other services rose from 3.6% to 6.3% of fee income
what_changed.text: Fees from PMS, AIF and other services grew from ₹44.60 crore in FY23 to ₹115.39 crore in FY26, about 37% a year, while asset management and advisory fees grew about 14% a year to ₹1,729.64 crore. Their share of consolidated fee income rose every year: 3.6%, 4.9%, 5.8%, 6.3%. Net of distributor commission the alternates share is smaller: management put it at about 6% gross and 3.5% net. The government mandates that lifted reported AUM in FY27 are not part of this change.
